subject: Re: PayGrid model-fit eval & parity discussion
messages:
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Samir Patel <samir@paygrid.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 15:15:00 +0000
Subject: PayGrid model-fit eval & parity discussion

Samir — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

Summary of needs:
- Primary goal: replace current proprietary semantic-ranking baseline with an open model stack while keeping precision on invoice/NLP extraction and reducing hallucination rates.
- Success metric: parity or better on end-to-end accuracy for the QA/regression prompt set PayGrid shared in the call; maintain or improve hallucination rate and keep latency within operational SLOs.

Recommended first-pass models (we'll run the evals and share results):
- Open candidates: Llama-2-13B-Instruct (int8), Mistral-Instruct-7B, and Falcon-40B-instruct (quantized profile)
- Redwood baseline for comparison: rwd-prop-1.0 (our tuned, production baseline)

What we need from PayGrid:
1) The prompt set and annotated expected outputs (attached: paygrid_prompt_set_v1.json)
2) A small sample of production queries (anonymized or schema-only if needed) for latency/throughput profiling
3) Your acceptance thresholds — we suggested parity defined as within 1.5% absolute on the primary accuracy metric and hallucination delta <1%, but happy to adjust.

Deliverables & timeline:
- Redwood to run batch evals across the three open candidates + rwd-prop-1.0 and share a benchmark report with p50/p95 latency, cost-per-1k-tokens, accuracy/F1, and hallucination metrics by Fri Jul 9.
- Follow-up customer deep-dive scheduled week of Jul 12 to walk results and discuss pilot if metrics are acceptable.

Attachments: paygrid_prompt_set_v1.json (prompt set + expected labels)
Related links: https://redwood-inference.app/evals/PG-2026-042/dashboard

Open questions for PayGrid (please reply):
- Confirm whether we can use a de-identified sample or need to operate on schema only for the first eval.
- Confirm acceptance thresholds (we proposed parity within 1.5%, hallucination delta <1%).
- Any preferred requirements for throughput/latency (p95 target) or deployment environment (dedicated vs hosted)?

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Enterprise Sales Lead, Redwood Inference

- Acceptance thresholds: 1.5% sounds reasonable as a starting point, but we need to be explicit about the primary metric. For us that's F1 on field extraction + a separate hallucination rate measured on a curated 500-record QA set. Can you confirm how you measure hallucination?

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Cc: Samir Patel <samir@paygrid.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 12:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: PayGrid model-fit eval & parity discussion — eval plan

Looping in the evaluation plan and metrics so Samir has visibility. High level plan: 

Models & profiles we will run (initial pass):
- rwd-prop-1.0 (Redwood tuned baseline) — reference
- Llama-2-13B-Instruct (int8 / kv-cache enabled)
- Mistral-Instruct-7B (int8 quantized profile)
- Falcon-40B-instruct (int8 / 4bit quant profiles for cost sensitivity)

Quantization / runtime notes:
- We'll include 8-bit and 4-bit profiles where supported; report both quality delta and cost/throughput tradeoffs.
- Runtime targets: run on A100 for accuracy baselines and on T4/GPU-class equivalent for predicted customer latency/cost.

Metrics & acceptance criteria:
- Primary metric: Macro F1 on annotated extraction tasks (PayGrid prompt set). Parity = within 1.5% absolute of rwd-prop-1.0 on primary metric.
- Hallucination metric: measured as percent of outputs containing unsupported facts on the 500-record QA test; target is delta <= 1% vs baseline.
- Latency: p50/p95 measured on representative 1-2k request batches; p95 target will be documented but Samir please confirm acceptable value (we often set p95 < 600ms for interactive use).
- Robustness: paraphrase sensitivity & prompt injection checks (we'll run a subset of adversarial prompts).

Deliverables and timeline:
- Jul 2: confirm anonymized sample & final prompt set (PayGrid)
- Jul 3-8: run batch evaluations across models and quant profiles
- Jul 9: deliver Redwood Eval Summary (PDF) + dashboard link
- Jul 12: follow-up 60-minute deep-dive to review results and next steps

Attachments: redwood_eval_summary.pdf (template and example results)
Related Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-paygrid-eval-template

Notes: If an open model meets parity within thresholds and has acceptable hallucination and latency, we recommend a 4-week pilot on Redwood Dedicated to validate in-production throughput and costs. I'll include a cost delta table in the Jul 9 deliverable.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Applied ML, Redwood Inference

Samir — thanks for the quick reply and for the security questionnaire. Confirming next steps and owners: 

Action items:
- PayGrid (Samir/Olivia): provide anonymized sample or confirm schema-only by Jul 2; return completed security questionnaire to security@redwood.ai.
- Redwood (Marissa + Infra): run evals across listed models and quant profiles, produce the Redwood Eval Summary by Jul 9. Include: accuracy/F1, hallucination rate, latency p50/p95 on both A100 and customer-grade GPUs, and cost-per-1M tokens.
- Redwood (Lauren): schedule deep-dive for week of Jul 12 — propose Tue Jul 13 or Wed Jul 14, 10:00–11:00 PT; will confirm once I see Samir's availability.
- Procurement: Samir — please share your procurement contact if we'd like to discuss pilot terms/discounts; we typically provide a pilot discount for parity validations.

Acceptance criteria recap: parity = within 1.5% absolute on primary F1 metric; hallucination delta <= 1% vs rwd-prop-1.0. If open models meet those thresholds and latency targets, we'll propose a 4-week Redwood Dedicated pilot to validate at-scale.

Looking forward — I can jump on a quick call if you want to walk through the prompt set together.

Best,
